briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Relief in Sight: Michigan's Tax Fight Turns a Corner as National Rescheduling and M&A Surge
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis tax fight is shifting from defense to offense — a bipartisan repeal push, a September trial date, and a new Ann Arbor storefront show operators finding daylight after a brutal first half. Nationally, DEA's rescheduling hearing transcript, a $272M MSO takeover bid, and fast-moving psilocybin science signal the industry's next chapter is about growth, not contraction.

local.text: Lume Cannabis Co. opened its new Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street with a three-day grand-opening celebration — fresh proof operators are still betting on Washtenaw County even as the statewide market tightens.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a 'Freedom Agenda' pledging to repeal or sharply roll back the 24% wholesale tax while cracking down on unlicensed hemp and illegal grow operations — a plank Democratic primary rival Chris Swanson has also embraced, meaning tax relief now has bipartisan momentum heading into November regardless of who wins the governor's mansion.

A bipartisan coalition of eight state senators is backing Senate Bill 810 to repeal Whitmer's Comprehensive Road Funding Tax Act outright, and at least one Democrat who originally voted for the tax, Sen. Rosemary Bayer, has flipped to co-sponsor the repeal — a sign support for relief is growing, not shrinking.

The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax is heading to trial in September, giving operators a concrete near-term shot at rolling back the levy through the courts after a judge kept the case alive.

Even after a rough first half, Michigan remains the nation's second-largest legal cannabis market — a resilience operators and lawmakers are now citing as the case for why the tax should come down rather than push the industry further underground.

national.text: The DEA released the full transcript of its cannabis rescheduling hearing, showing government lawyers arguing plainly that 'marijuana can no longer remain in Schedule I' — the clearest public evidence yet that the federal case for moving cannabis to Schedule III is advancing.

The rescheduling docket cleared another procedural checkpoint on August 18, with a formal proposed rule now expected before year-end 2026 and a final rule possible in 2027 — a change that would gut the 280E tax penalty that currently pushes effective rates on operators as high as 60%.

Curaleaf formally launched its $272 million hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, offering a 45% premium that would hand the U.S. MSO more than 50 tons of additional EU-GMP medical cultivation capacity — the boldest sign yet that consolidation, not contraction, defines the industry's next phase.

Tilray Brands is expanding medical cannabis cultivation across Quebec and Portugal, lifting global annual production capacity to roughly 275 metric tons from 210 to keep pace with rising international demand.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin program keeps clearing hurdles: with the FDA finalizing its psychedelic trial guidance and scheduling a September 14 public hearing on psychedelic therapeutics, Compass is targeting an NDA submission for COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression and commercial launch-readiness by the end of 2026.
